channel.title: Wire — Engineering
channel.description: Engineering from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: Supporting native Rust in Workers with the new Emscripten target for wasm-bindgen
item.description: With the new experimental support for the Emscripten target in Rust Workers, many previously unsupported Rust libraries and applications can now be built and deployed directly to Cloudflare’s global Workers platform, including upcoming… (2 sources: cloudflare, rprogramming)

item.title: Introducing cf: the agentic CLI for the entire Cloudflare API
item.description: We are releasing cf, our new command-line tool that mirrors the entire Cloudflare API and supports programmatic TypeScript configuration. We are also open-sourcing Forge, our internal SDK generator. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: Four months of VoidZero at Cloudflare: making the open-source JavaScript toolchain faster for all humans and agents
item.description: Since joining Cloudflare, VoidZero has delivered more than 80 releases that drastically speed up JavaScript compilation, linting, and testing. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: How fast is the web? Explore billions of real-user measurements with BEACON
item.description: Cloudflare is open-sourcing the BEACON dataset, making billions of anonymized Real User Monitoring (RUM) performance records publicly available on Google BigQuery. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: Next.js applications, powered by Vite: introducing Vinext 1.0
item.description: Vinext 1.0 graduates from an AI experiment to a production-ready framework, letting developers run Next.js apps on Vite. This release brings advanced cache warming, broader compatibility, and an automated testing pipeline. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: Introducing Forge: the open source pipeline for generating SDKs, CLIs, docs, and more
item.description: Forge is a pluggable, open-source pipeline that runs in CI to generate SDKs, CLIs, and documentation directly from API definitions. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: Highlights from Git 2.56
item.description: The open source Git project just released Git 2.56. Here is GitHub's look at some of the most interesting features and changes introduced since last time. The post Highlights from Git 2.56 appeared first on The GitHub Blog . (1 source: githubblog)

item.title: Atlassian Rebuilds Metrics Pipeline Around OpenTelemetry at Massive Scale
item.description: Software company Atlassian has published an account of its migration from gostatsd to OpenTelemetry, replacing the internal workings of a metrics platform that receives data from about 100,000 hosts across 14 regions. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: The problem is not AI code, but not knowing about system architecture or intent
item.description: If we think writing code is dead, and AI is generating all codebases, I still think the bigger problem is people or full teams not knowing anything anymore about the system... (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: How we found 24 Android vulnerabilities using our open source AI security agent
item.description: A look at the targeted AI taskflows behind these findings, the critical Android bugs they uncovered, and how to run the same open-source agent on your own app. (1 source: githubblog)

item.title: Travel’s AI dilemma at Skift Global Forum
item.description: At the “great recalibration”-themed travel conference, Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky called AI “an existential risk” to his company and “literally the best thing to ever happen” to it in the same discussion. (1 source: stripe)
